## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Adopt mode should be fixed so that it stops reporting a change and rewriting the file when the incoming value already equals the stored one, because the module docstring says `merge` preserves untouched configuration files.

## Changes
The pull request adds an `adopt` flag to `merge` in `app/config.py` that overwrites every existing key present in `incoming` and records it as a change, and restructures the `replace` branch into a nested condition. It adds one test for adoption and one for replacement of a differing value, plus an unused `REVIEW_CONTEXT` constant in `tests/test_config.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — correctness — Adopt mode rewrites the file when values already match — `merge(path, {"theme": "dark"}, adopt=True)` on a file containing `{"theme":"dark"}\n` returns `["theme"]` and rewrites the file with `indent=2`. The `adopt` branch omits the `current[key] != value` check that the `replace` branch applies at `app/config.py:19`. — Callers are told a setting changed when it did not, and an untouched file is reformatted, contrary to the module docstring. — Fix: Guard the assignment with `current[key] != value`, or, if adoption must list unchanged keys, write the file only when a value changed; extend `test_unchanged_replacement_preserves_bytes` with an `adopt=True` case.
